utterances.text: I just try to speed up things, to find out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, but you don't have to give evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell us, please: Based on these results, what was the conclusion? What transpired?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: What transpired is that certain deputies - I don't know whether it was because they didn't know who those people were or they just simply didn't vote, these two candidates who were there. However, what happened at the assembly meeting, that's what the result of the vote was, so I can't see what else I should add.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you add up the three groups of votes, 32, 17, and 3, respectively, what do you get? What's the result? If you compare to what you can see on page 1, what can you state about that? What's your conclusion, if you add up all the votes which you see here and the number of those present?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: 17, 14 -- well, I think this is 54 votes, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was never very good at maths, but my calculation shows 32, 17, and 3, which adds up to 52.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. 52. I'm sorry. Yes, yes, yes, 52 votes. And the conclusion was that the number of those present, the total of those present, was 53.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge if the political parties operated in 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: I don't think I understood your question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. In 1992, throughout 1992, did -- was the work of the political parties done?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: Were political parties actually active? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what I mean.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the work of the political parties being frozen in that period?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: I believe it was up to April or May, and then the activity of all political parties -- the activities of all political parties were frozen in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your personal political view about that period, well, ever since that period and up to this very day?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: After the activities of the political parties were frozen, I was no longer involved in politics after that. I never went back to politics, and, well, the kind of time that that was, well, you know, it was impossible to work in any normal kind of way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you a member of any party nowadays?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal information as to whether Mr. Blagoje Simic, following this meeting, this session, ever had any specific tasks or duties within the framework of the Northern Bosnia SAO?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, Dr. Blagoje Simic had no specific tasks in Northern Bosnia, aside from his formal appointment as vice-president. Nothing else that I know of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please: How often did you actually see Dr. Blagoje Simic? How often have you seen him since, or how often did you see him between that period in April and May 1993? Just try to cover that period approximately.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: I think in 1991, maybe in 1992, at the beginning of 1992, we did meet two or three times. We had some talks and there were some meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber about your contact in that period. Dr. Blagoje Simic, did he display any particular views concerning ethnic intolerance? Did he voice any extremist political views against other ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: I had known Mr. Blagoje Simic from before, from the former government when I held an official position in Gracanica municipality and he in Samac. We had some economic cooperation. There was a certain amount of activity. And then the hard times came for everyone in Bosnia and Herzegovina. But I never once noticed or observed that Dr. Blagoje Simic ever displayed any signs of intolerance or discrimination against other ethnic groups. Not a single sign, in any way, or in any area in which we cooperated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear from any of the people you met that Blagoje Simic displayed any kind of intolerant or discriminatory behaviour?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Counsel is testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree, yes. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please tell the Trial Chamber: In your contact with other people, people you were meeting, did they talk about Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of that, and I assert that the people I used to meet later on in the following period, after I -- when I had no more contact with Dr. Blagoje Simic, I had no inkling of any sort of - what should I call it - intolerance of other ethnic groups or any other activity indicating anything that was not normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Marusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Finished with this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any other questions? I see none. Can the Prosecution cross-examine, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Weiner:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Marusic. My name is Phillip Weiner and I'm going to ask you questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You can leave that document there. We might be referring to it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go right to that meeting in Doboj on the 4th of November, 1991. At that meeting there was an election and you remember the elections that occurred from memory as opposed to that document; isn't that true? Isn't that --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: I remember that those elections took place, but I cannot or I couldn't remember all these figures, and I could not remember the number of delegates that were present. I hope you understand that quite some time has elapsed since then. What I stated in my statement could also be erroneous from time to time, but I think that before -- I think that I said from 50 to 60 delegates, whereas now I see from this document that there must have been approximately 53.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That doesn't make a difference. The question I have for you is: You remember that Nikola Perisic was elected president of the SAO of Northern Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Nikola Perisic was elected for president of the SAO Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then after that they had election of the vice-presidents; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. During that same assembly, on that same day when it was convened, the president was elected, the vice-president was elected, as well as the secretary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the two vice-presidents that were elected were Milovan Bjelosevic of Derventa and the defendant Blagoje Simic of Bosanski Samac; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Milovan Bjelosevic was one of the vice-presidents that was elected and Dr. Blagoje Simic was the second vice-president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you knowing Dr. Blagoje Simic, did you congratulate him after being elected vice-president, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, as well as I congratulated the president and the second vice-president. I did congratulate everybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were elected at that meeting or at a later meeting as president or Prime Minister of the SAO, or the person responsible to get the government functioning. Was it at that meeting or at a later meeting?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: No, not at that meeting. I cannot recall the exact date at the present moment, but I believe that it must have been a month later, or maybe 20 days after that meeting. I do not remember the date, unfortunately. However, I was elected. I was appointed and elected as the Prime Minister of SAO Northern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And was Dr. Blagoje Simic at that meeting when you were elected as Prime Minister, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: I do not recall if Mr. Blagoje Simic was there at the time. Maybe there was somebody from the municipality of Samac. But on that day, I do not recall if Mr. Blagoje Simic was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you became Prime Minister and had to establish a government, did you ever speak to the defendant Blagoje Simic about his role as vice-president or plans for the -- plans or thoughts or ideas for this government?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: I never spoke to Dr. Blagoje Simic, nor about his position as the vice-president, nor did we discuss any plans with regards to the programmes or the planning of my future government. During that session, I didn't even know most of those delegates. I just very briefly exposed my programme and my plans pertaining -- my work in that government, and I explained what I thought I should do as a Prime Minister of SAO Northern Bosnia autonomous region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question doesn't concern at that meeting. Any time after did you pick up the telephone and call either the president Nikola Perisic or the two vice-presidents and talk to them about plans for the region, talk to them about the roles that they had as president and vice-presidents? Did you ever do that any time after your election, a week later, two weeks later, a month later?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did have a few discussions with Mr. Perisic, as the president of the Municipal Assembly. I deemed that it was necessary to consult most of municipalities that became part of the SAO Northern Bosnia. I wanted to know which people were to do certain positions or should be candidated or nominated for certain positions with respect to their professions, so that we can see what were the best positions for them. And as of that day, Mr. Perisic was practically, as the number-one person in the assembly, to consult most of these municipalities as to nominate a certain number of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever speak to vice-president Simic about any of these plans or ideas?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: With the vice-president, Mr. Simic, I never spoke about the composition of the government. I stated earlier that Mr. Perisic was in charge to get in touch with all the municipalities and to submit to me the list of certain people who would be working in the government. So I do claim that Mr. Blagoje was not involved in the work of the government, and I did not consult him with regards to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you never spoke to him concerning any work after he was, in your terms, formally elected vice-president? You never did, but Mr. Perisic did?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: I cannot claim this. Mr. Perisic could confirm it to you probably, because he got in touch with the officials of the municipality and he was the one who was to appoint or to nominate certain people who would be working in the government of the SAO Northern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the other matter I want to talk to you: You gave your opinion as to the views or activities of Blagoje Simic. After the war started, you eventually moved to Doboj, the municipality of Doboj; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: That is correct. Up until the beginning of the war, I was the president of the Executive Board of the municipality of Gracanica, which is part of the Federation, which was constituted after the Dayton Accord. And then I started living in Doboj. I was living in the apartment of my uncle, and I had reported to the Red Cross as a refugee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Doboj was a distance from Samac, about 50 kilometres or more? A good distance, would you say?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: I think that it's between 50 to 80 kilometres. That's the distance from Doboj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during 1992 or, let's say, from April 17th on of 1992 and during 1993, you were travelling on a regular basis to Samac, were you?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: No. I never travelled to Samac. I don't know where did you get this. I was a refugee and I spent my time in Doboj. And excuse me if I may add: I was never involved with politics any more. I was never involved in politics, I was never involved in establishing the government, and I was not involved in questions regarding the SAO Northern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So sir, is it -- you never -- you had never travelled during those almost two years to Samac. Is it fair to say, then, that you were not closely following the day-to-day activities of the Crisis Staff and War Presidency in Samac while you were living in Doboj in 1992 and 1993? Is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is quite fair to say that I had not seen Mr. Blagoje Simic. I was not following the work of the organs that were active in the municipality of Samac, nor was I following the work of other organs of other municipalities. I was simply outside of politics, aside from the fact that of course, as an observer and as a man, I had some knowledge which I was able to get from some sources which I would say whether -- I don't know if I -- those sources were the media, whether it was the radio or the television, but I was able to get information from the media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just continue. I'll ask you some questions and you can just answer yes or no. Would you also agree it's fair to say that you weren't following closely the day-to-day activities of the defendant Blagoje Simic in Samac in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: I had some problems with the interpretation. Would you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure, sir. So is it fair to say, would you agree with me that in 1992 and 1993, you weren't following the day-to-day activities of the defendant Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: I should say that after the month of May, I did not follow the day-to-day activities of Dr. Blagoje Simic, but up until that date, during the time while I was an active member of the Executive Board in Gracanica, I was mandated by the government of Northern Bosnia, I should say that at the time I knew what Mr. Blagoje Simic was doing and I had stated this in my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I just want to ask you questions about certain periods. So once again, is it fair to say, sir, that you weren't following, from May on of 1992, let's say from the end of April on of 1992 you weren't following the day-to-day activities, happenings, occurrences, actions, in Bosanski Samac? Isn't that fair to say too?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is fair to say, aside from the fact that I was following the media. I was hearing what was going on in that area on the television, on the radio, and I know that the municipality of Samac was surrounded and that later the events that took place which were linked to the autonomous region of Semberija and Majevica, and that the municipality of Samac was very active within that organisation of municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you received only limited news about Samac, were you aware that the Crisis Staff in Bosanski Samac had established a charitable foundation and named it after a Serbian paramilitary, nicknamed Vuk? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware in early May of a mass murder in Crkvina, which is a small village outside of the town of Samac, where 16 non-Serb civilians were killed and it was committed by the same Serbian paramilitaries? Were you aware of that in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: No. This is the first time I hear this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware that the defendant Blagoje Simic issued a letter on behalf -- issued a letter of appreciation and a letter of commendation to the town of Vranje on behalf of the leader of the Serbian paramilitaries that was serving in Samac? Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: No. I was not able to find that information anywhere, nor through the television or through the media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware that a decision was issued by the Crisis Staff in May of 1992 to isolate all persons of Croat nationality? Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. If the news was not broadcast over the radio or the television, I was not able to find that out, and I didn't have any other sources which would inform me of these facts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's continue. Were you aware that hundreds of non-Serb civilians, including men, women, children, and elderly, were isolated at facilities in Samac? Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And not being a regular visitor to Samac in 1992, you were not aware of the conditions in the prison camps and detention facilities there; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: Well, to be very honest with you, I must tell you that the events that transpired later were not getting to me. I was not able to find out about them. I was not particularly interested in it either, since the body -- where it used to be mandatory was not operational any more. I had no other contacts and there was no need for me to go to Samac. And there was no need for me to try to find out what was going on in Samac either. Now, if this happened, if this took place in Samac, I don't know. I don't know who was behind it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So basically, you weren't aware, from May of 1992 on, what was happening in Bosanski Samac as to day-to-day activities, as well as the activities of the Crisis Staff and the War Presidency; you had no awareness of any activities?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: No. We had no contacts whatsoever at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And similarly, you had no information as to the activities of Dr. Blagoje Simic, the defendant in this case, during that same period; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV MARUSIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much for giving evidence to the Trial Chamber. We are now finished. You are free to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please stand up and make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Yes, Mr. Pantelic. Just for the particulars. Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will rather do that, Your Honour, but I think there is rulings of this Trial Chamber that only cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but just for the record, his particulars.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. In the moment, I was so happy to get the opportunity, but it seems that I was not happy, lucky enough. Examined by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Jovanovic. Could you please state your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Simo Jovanovic. My father's name is Stevo, my mother's name is Ana.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit D173/1 for this witness, just to verify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were born on 5th April 1962, and all the personal data in your statement are correct; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a member of the army of Republika Srpska. You were a member of the special detachment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any additional education or qualifications? Did you attend any courses in the area of security or military doctrines?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In 1993 I attended a security and intelligence course in Pancevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic. Just for the sake of clarity. On page 57, line 16, the witness -- sorry - your question was: "You were a member of the special detachment." Is "detachment" the right word or should it be "battalion"? I'm just -- if you could just clarify so that we get the right word in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're talking about a special battalion?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In other words -- it is a special battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that course that you attended for security and intelligence services, were you familiarised with some procedures and regulations that rule the work of the army and the police? Was that one part of your course?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have some personal knowledge about the functioning of the hierarchy in the military security?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think that is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examination can proceed. Are there any counsel that wish to ask this witness any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Pisarevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Jovanovic. I'm going to ask you a few questions that arise from your statement. As the two of us speak the same language, please hear me out first, make a pause, and then start answering my question. Here I have your statement that you gave according to 92 bis Rule, and as I can see here, you stated that you served in the JNA in 1972 and 1973, in Pristina. Tell me, please: After the compulsory military service, or during the service, did you acquire a rank of a reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't acquire any ranks. I wasn't awarded any ranks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the period between 1983 and 1992, were you awarded any reserve officer's rank?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was proposed by the command, but I was never actually awarded a promotion by my Superior Command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: In what part of the military did you serve when you were in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was a member of an infantry unit first. That's where I did my training. And after that I went to Kicevo, where I was additionally trained to be a driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here in your statement you also spoke about your life. You said that you were a profession footballer and that you were a member of the Jedinstvo football club from Brcko. How long did you spend playing football in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That was between 1985 and the outbreak of conflicts in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. In the meantime, I spent one year playing football for the Samac-based Borac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were playing football, and while you had your professional obligations as a football player, were you officially a permanent resident of Brcko and recorded as such by the police?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not a resident, a permanent resident of Brcko. My native place was some 20 kilometres away from Brcko, so I commuted every day when I had to go to Brcko to play football or to do my training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said, in paragraph 4 of your statement, that on the 10th of October, 1991, you were mobilised as a member of the Territorial Defence in Obudovac and that you were mobilised by the secretariat for National Defence in Samac. Can you please clarify that. As far as I know, the Territorial Defence, as a segment of the armed forces of the then Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, did not exist at that time. Where were you actually mobilised? What actually happened? What call-up papers did you actually receive?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does say here that I was mobilised into the Territorial Defence. However, this is a mistake. I was mobilised into a JNA unit which was stationed in Obudovac. This is a mistake in the way my statement was recorded. It was not the Territorial Defence. It was the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Tell me: What was the name of that unit that you were assigned to?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember its exact name. It's been a long time ago. It was 10 or 11 years ago. I know that the commander of that unit was Mr. -- Captain, rather, Subotin. And it was a JNA unit. And I can't provide you with any more detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. When you mentioned Captain Subotin, do you mean Captain Marko Subotin?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is who I mean, Marko Subotin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. And here also you stated that you were assigned to the command of the military police. What exactly was your assignment when you were mobilised into that unit? What did you do in that unit? Can you please be more specific.

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. What do you mean by that? Can you repeat?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your duties and tasks? What was your detachment? So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now I understand. When I was mobilised by the secretariat of National Defence, I reported to the command, to Captain Marko Subotin and he told me to go to the military police detachment, which was stationed in Obudovac. Our tasks at that time were to provide security for the command post and to provide security for the commander. We would also accompany the commander when he went to certain meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. Thank you. If I understood you well, you provided the security for the command post of the unit under the command of Captain Marko Subotin and also to accompany or escort Captain Marko Subotin as the commander of that unit. You were his official escorts as he moved about the territory of Samac municipality and generally across Bosnia and Herzegovina. Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you did understand me well. That was not in every single case, but as per commander's orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. You stated here that at one point in time, you became the deputy of the commander. Were you talking about the detachment of the military police? A platoon of the military police? What kind of an establishment was that with the command in Obudovac?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As I've said, this was a detachment, and I became the -- or a squad. I became the deputy when the 17th Tactical Group was established. I don't remember whether that was in late January or early February, 1992. I only know that I was the commander of that squad, which then became a platoon, and the commander of the detachment of the military police was Mr. Jovan Erletic and his state was in Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, with your company, you remained in Obudovac and you were under the immediate command of Captain Marko Subotin?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, when we became a company, that is, when I -- when my platoon joined the military company -- military police company, our immediate commander was Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic, and the orders that I received, I received mostly via Captain Marko Subotin and the commander of the military police, obviously. But mostly those orders were received via Captain Marko Subotin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have not answered part of my question that was raised to the place where you were stationed: Did you continue being stationed in the command post of the commander, that is, Captain Marko Subotin in Obudovac?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were stationed in Obudovac, and when necessary and as per commander Nikolic's orders we would be sent elsewhere to perform tasks. In February 1992, one part of my military police went to provide security for the tank brigade. I don't know on what axis, but I know that their passage had to be secured towards Brod. I was not there, so I can't give you any detail. And I know that their commander was Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, a little while ago you said that you received your orders exclusively from the commander of the military police company and that you mostly received orders via your commander, Mr. -- Captain Marko Subotin. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Let me just explain to the Trial -- to the Honourable Chamber. There was a lack of communication, and the military police particularly did not have enough means of communication, so the communication went from Pelagicevo via Obudovac, and I don't see anything disputable in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive orders from the commander of the 17th Tactical Group, Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that between you, as the commander of a platoon and the commander Nikolic, there were other command structures as the commander of the military police company, your command, the deputy commander for security, and so on and so forth? So they were people in between, there were structures between you, as the company commander, and the commander of the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were at the time such structures, because that's the way things functioned at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pisarevic. I'd just like to get a clarification from Mr. Jovanovic. Mr. Jovanovic, you stated, on page 62, lines 9 and 10, in an answer to a question from Mr. Pisarevic, and I'll quote. You say: "Our immediate commander was Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic." And then you went on and said that you received orders mostly via Captain Marko Subotin. Now, later, on page 63, lines 7 and 8, Mr. Pisarevic asked you: "Did you receive orders from the commander of the 17th Tactical Group, Nikolic?" And your answer is no. So I wonder whether you can clarify those two answers. In the first instance, you mention Nikolic, and then you say you received orders mostly via an obvious subordinate to Nikolic, Captain Marko Subotin. But now in the second response, you simply say no, you didn't get any orders from Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic. So if you could just try and clarify what seems to be a bit of an inconsistency there between the two answers, if I'm reading them correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe I've understood your question. As I said a while ago, the chain of command, according to the chain of command, I was directly subordinated to Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic. However, the orders that came from the command of the 17th Tactical Group came via lower-ranking units and subordinate commanders, through Captain Marko Subotin. As for the use of police forces, Marko Subotin coordinated this with, I suppose, Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So were any of the orders that you received emanating from Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic being passed through Captain Marko Subotin, as a conduit of the order? So were the orders coming from the top, being relayed to this Captain, and maybe others, and then eventually coming to you through this chain of command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely. In order for me to receive my tasks, I should go to Pelagicevo every day, travel there, and Pelagicevo is not near Obudovac. So we used protected communications to forward information that was essential at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So therefore, your response to the second question that I mentioned from Mr. Pisarevic: Did you receive orders from the command of the 17th Tactical Group, Nikolic? And you said no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but through Captain Marko Subotin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. That puts it in a clear perspective now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, let us try to, well, clarify this. Your commander, Marko Subotin, could he give you orders, and was he actually issuing orders to you?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure about whether he could --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but did he actually?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the orders at that time were only to provide security for the command building, to go here, go there, report to the command of the 17th Tactical Group, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... of the assistant registrar, please. You can proceed, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The commander of the military police company, did he give you orders?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your commander, Marko Subotin, while issuing regular orders, tell you -- well, here. This is an order which came straight from the commander of the 17th Tactical Group, Stevan Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As I said a while ago in my testimony, at one point in time Captain Marko Subotin called me and said that he had received orders from Lieutenant Colonel Stevan Nikolic, for me to take part of my unit and report to Pelagicevo for a reinforced squad to be set up there and that we should go there and carry out the task, as ordered by Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the only time?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. At some point in the month of March, he called me again and sent me to report to the command post at Pelagicevo; more specifically, to Captain first class, I believe, Makso Simeunovic. There was a task that needed carrying out in the area of the zone of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Makso Simeunovic, what was he? What did he do, the person you were supposed to report to at the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simeunovic was the chief of security of the 17th Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever in a position to see a written order issued to you by Mr. Stevan Nikolic, the commander of the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you look at item 5 of your statement, please. I assume there is a slight imprecision there, but we need to clarify this. You said, towards the end of April 1992, at the proposal of Marko Subotin, from the command of the 17th TG, from the command of the Tactical Group. So what I understand is that here you are asserting that Marko Subotin was actually a member of the command of the 17th Tactical Group. To the best of your knowledge and recollection, Marko Subotin, was he a member of the command of the 17th Tactical Group or not?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Frankly, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, Mr. Jovanovic, if you could please find paragraph 13 of your statement, on page 5. It reads as follows: "Also they were told that upon arrival and upon occupying their positions, they should establish communications with the other forces and units of the 17th Tactical Group, units that would also be deployed in the same area, and that activities should be coordinated with the 4th Detachment, which was already in the area." That's your statement. I have a number of questions related to this. When you arrived in the customs-free zone, whom did you find there?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: When I reached the main buildings of the customs-free zone - that was my original destination - I found a JNA unit there, Yugoslav People's Army unit, from, I believe, anti-armour company from Srpska Tisina, and a number of other soldiers were there whom I didn't know, several. I did recognise a number of people who were there, because we are from the same municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Jovanovic. In your statement, you said: "I believe they were members of the TO, or Territorial Defence." Again, what do you mean by "TO"? Do you mean this, whatever you called it, company or unit, anti-armour, from the village of Tisina?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, but there's a mistake there. These were JNA members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you also found a number of persons wearing camouflage uniforms. Did you recognise those persons who were wearing camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, you said: "And then they retreated to the town, back to their units." Can you tell us, please: Who was it that retreated back into town or to their units to carry out other tasks when you came? Are we talking about the persons who were wearing camouflage uniforms or are we talking about JNA members?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I stayed in the positions where I found them, and I set up the communications equipment there. And they headed all together down the railroad track leading to the town, or rather, leading towards the road leading into the town. We know very well that when there, once you reach the road, you can head straight into town or you can head back into Tisina, the village of Tisina, but they told me expressly that they were headed back into town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here, quite obviously, we have two separate groups of persons. Which was the group telling you that they would head back into town?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was in the morning, and the weather was bad. I remember quite clearly. I can't tell you precisely which group, but I know they went together --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't say, just tell us you can't say. It's no problem at all.

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I simply don't remember. It was dark there and there was no electricity there. There was nothing there. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, I was just going to say to

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: If the translation is correct, and you said now twice, "They headed all together down the railroad track leading to the town," does "they headed all together" mean members of the two groups, the JNA and the men in the camouflage uniforms, or not? We seem to have some confusion in some of the answers here. So maybe if you could clarify what you mean by when you said "they headed all together down the railroad track leading to the town." MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, and as a supplement to what Your Honour has just raised now, there's -- the witness started to say: "It was the morning, the weather was bad. I remember quite clearly. It's not clear in the transcript. He then says precisely which group, but I know they went together, and then he was cut off by Mr. Pisarevic. So again, there's a second reference to them, two groups going together. And I suggest that that also arises from Your Honour's question

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honours. It seems that this is a good time for a break, so perhaps we should resume after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll take our break and continue at 12.50 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will have to wait for the accused persons, since they didn't consent to our proceeding in their absence. We just take it that they should be on their way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We see that everybody is here now. We can start.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, before the break you were asked to explain how is it that these people left, those members, as you called them, members wearing camouflage uniforms, members of that particular detachment, anti-armoured detachment, company, rather. If you cannot remember how it all took place, please tell us that you don't remember; or if you do tell us, did they leave together? You said they went down the railroad tracks?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did say that they went down the railroad track, but I don't recall anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Do you know where is it that they went?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You and that squad that arrived to that duty-free zone, or custom-free zone, did you ever receive some kind of an order to go into the city of Samac?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I never received the order to go into Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever enter into Samac with your squad?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, not with my squad, and I don't really know what you're asking me. The question is not very clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the 16th and 17th. During those two days, did you and your squad enter the city of Samac on the 17th and on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, because I was not in that position, and I did not receive that order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pisarevic. Mr. Jovanovic, you said before the break, in response to a question from Mr. Pisarevic, and this is on page 68, lines 11 to 15, you said that they were on the railway tracks and so on. And you went on to say: "But they told me expressly that they were headed back into town." And just now you've been asked a question, on page 70, lines 10 and following, or line 13, Mr. Pisarevic says to you: "Do you know where that is they went?" And you said: "No, I don't know." So which is the correct answer? The one before we took the break or this one? Again we need some clarity for the transcript there on that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it could be a translation problem. What I wanted to ask is: Did you see where they went. I wanted to know if the witness has any direct knowledge as to where they went. I wanted to know if he knows if they went into town. And if I understood him correctly, the witness said that he did not see them going into town; not that he didn't know, but that he didn't see them. But I will clarify this with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: You see, I think it was the way the question was. You asked him, at least in the English: Do you know? And he said: No, I don't. So it wasn't a question of eyesight in the question as posed in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting you, but I thought we were talking about the town of Samac, and now we are talking about a city of Gracenac. Where are we?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is in the city of Samac, as far as I know. I think there's a mistake in the transcript. It is not the city of Gracenac; rather, the city of Samac. We are in Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I hope so. MR. DI FAZIO: I was mystified as well, with respect, if Your Honours please. Can we assume that every reference in the last minute or two or three minutes to Samac has been a mistake and that in fact the transcript should reflect Samac?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Can we assume that? Because I assume that's correct, because the witness has never spoken about Samac at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, we are talking about the city of Samac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us: Did you see if those men who left you, did they go to the city of Samac? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I already said that it was in the early morning hours. It was raining, and the rain was mixed with snow. It was also dark. And they left along the railroad tracks, and those tracks lead into the city. Now, where it is they went after the crossroad, I really don't know, because I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you arrived to that duty-free zone, in the morning hours of the 17th and during that day, did you coordinate or did you communicate with the command post of the 4th Detachment and did you also get in touch with members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, not that day. I didn't see anybody from the 4th Detachment. My only contact was through the transmission lines, communication lines, was -- that I was able to get in touch with Aco Jankovic up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the last part of the answer was: Aco Jankovic, who was at the top of silo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, please tell us only -- or rather, give us only answers to my question, and my following question is to the effect whereas if you know who replaced you and your company on that -- at that position, and after how many days were you replaced?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: My squad was replaced by the members of the 4th Detachment. I think that it was around the 20th or around the 21st. I cannot remember, because many years have gone since.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jovanovic, do you know: What were the tasks of the 4th Detachment, and which were the lines of defence that the members of the 4th Detachment occupied?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I do not know this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear from anyone that the members of the 4th Detachment, in any way, shape, or form, took part in the occupation of the city of Samac?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know this, because I was where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know this fact: Do you know when the army of the Republika Srpska was established?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I do not recall the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm the fact that Colonel Djurdjevic was, for a short period of time, the commander of the 2nd Posavinska Brigade and Infantry, Posavinska Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I knew that at the time there was a new commander who had arrived, a certain colonel, but I don't know who. I don't know how long he was there and I don't know how he got to be there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if, at the end of the month of May, a commander was appointed for the 2nd Infantry Posavinska Brigade, a commander by the name of Dragan Djurdjevic?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know: Where were you deployed? In what military formation?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, I was deployed in the unit which was an intervention team, and they were to go where we had to block the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Tell us: Who was the commander of this intervention platoon?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: For what period of time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The period going from the end of the month of May up until the time it existed, June, July, or August. I don't know if it was still active in August.

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was Captain Josic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it Mr. Milan Josic who was the Captain from Obudovac?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever, during that period of time, deployed in the military police, or did you work in the security organ of the 2nd Posavina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me: Did you work in the military police or did you work in the security organ?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: For a short period of time, I worked at the military police; and at the time, it was -- it had its command post in Pelagicevo. And very quickly I got transferred into the organ of security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the assistant deputy of the commander for information and intelligence when you started working in the organ of security?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was Captain Jez, Zdravko Jez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Captain Jez was soon removed and arrested after that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you when Captain Jez was assistant commander for security and intelligence?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, I discharged the duties of an intelligence officer in the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, the Trial Chamber is wondering, especially the last few questions, how they help the defence of your client. And you've had what is considered to be sufficient time. Some of the questions you're asking are actually in the statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I had to mention Mr. Jez, who is not mentioned, because this helps my client's defence because in the information of the 13 signatories, as we call it here, this event is mentioned, and that is why I wanted to check that with Mr. Jovanovic, who was there. Thank you very much. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I just think for the record, in the English version here, 76, line 3, presumably it should read 13 signatories, not 13 submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It should be signatories, yes. Yes. We can proceed with the Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We shall continue sitting until we finish with this witness. We intend to proceed at 1415 so that he can finish his evidence and leave. MR. DI FAZIO: Do you mean go beyond 1415 or just adjourn briefly at that stage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Adjourn briefly then start again at 1415. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm mindful of that and I'll speed it up as much as I can, if Your Honours please. Cross-examined by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You joined the SDS when? I'm sorry. I didn't hear your answer. When did you join the SDS?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the date, but at the time I was not engaged anywhere and I joined, I believe that it was in 1990 or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In Obudovac. But you can't recall when, when in 1990?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Obudovac, but I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you remained a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw the SDS carrying out its policies in Bosanski Samac throughout 1992, 1993, 1994, and in the years thereafter. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I know that the work of the party was frozen during 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise to my learned friend. In order not to confuse the witness, maybe my learned friend can be more specific. In which kind of policies? Official programme, statute of the SDS, meetings, rallies, or something else? I mean, otherwise term "policies" is very, very broad term, and I think it might confuse this witness. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: With respect, it isn't, and I don't wish to waste much time on the topic. "Policies" is a clear word. It's understood in many languages and countries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. Carry on. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw nothing in the implementation of SDS policies between 1992 and recent times that have caused you any misgivings about it?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you: From the time I joined the army, both the 17th Tactical Group, the JNA, and the army of Republika Srpska, I did not engage in any politics. I just carried out orders of my Superior Command. I was not at all interested in politics at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let's turn to your statement. You have it there before you. And I'd like you to look at paragraph 13. There you're talking about events on the night of the 16th of April, prior to your going to Bosanski Samac in the middle of the night, and you say that one of the tasks that you were given was to go up and take your position on the Sava and that you were told, told, to establish communication with other forces and units of the 17th Tactical Group and coordinate your activity with the 4th Detachment that was already there. Do you see that passage in about midway through paragraph 13?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Now, in order to establish communication with other forces and units of the 17th Tactical Group, you had to know what other forces and units of the 17th Tactical Group were there. So tell the Trial Chamber what other forces and units of the 17th Tactical Group were operating in Bosanski Samac on the night of the 16th and 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, in Samac there was the civilian police and - how should I put it - some dozen or so guys who came from Serbia, as volunteers. They were in the town of Samac. There were some 15 of them or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So officers of the JNA, the command of the 17th Tactical Group, instructed you, prior to going to Bosanski Samac, to establish communications with police and paramilitaries who had come from Serbia. That was a specific instruction that you received prior to your going to the Sava to take up your position. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I did not receive any instructions as to the effect to link up with those units, but with the units of the JNA, and my contacts, the contacts that I established, were with some units that were active in that area. But those were JNA units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you a few moments ago was that -- I asked you to tell the Trial Chamber what forces and units of the 17th Tactical Group were operating in Bosanski Samac on the night of the 16th and 17th. You replied: "In Samac, there was the civilian police and the dozen or so guys from Serbia." Were you not implying that they were part of the 17th Tactical Group or part of the armed forces that you had to establish contact with in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Fine. Well, you tell the Chamber what you were informed about, what you were told you were to do with respect to these 15 or so guys from Serbia and the civilian police. What were your orders that you received in respect of those two groups on the night of the 16th?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as Samac is concerned, I did not receive any orders or anything like that in order for me to link up with them. The only order I received was to link up with the anti-armour battalion and with the 4th Detachment, because the 4th Detachment was in the town of Samac and its command post was in town itself. As for the other groups, I did not have anything whatsoever to do with them, the civilian police did their job, and the army did their job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Then tell the Trial Chamber of the JNA units that you were ordered to link up with. Which JNA units were you ordered to link up with, apart from the 4th Detachment, of course?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: With the anti-armour unit from Srpska Tisina, which was deployed in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the only other unit, apart from the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned that you had orders to link up with other JNA units. You've mentioned two: 4th Detachment and this anti-armour unit, anti-armour unit, two formations. Did you have orders to communicate with any other units or formations of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I'm talking -- I'm saying that I did receive an order to stop the Croatian forces which were about to cross over to the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The army at that time was in charge. That is, I was in charge of going to the border of Bosnia and Herzegovina to prevent the Croatian forces from entering the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. That's no problem. But I think you misunderstand me. I'm talking about the night of the 16th, before you would even go to the Sava. You've told us that you received orders to link up with JNA forces in Bosanski Samac, and we know of two groupings: The 4th Detachment and the anti-armour unit. On the night of the 16th, did you receive orders to link up with any other JNA units apart from those two?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not receive such an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So we're clear now. Your orders were clear: Link up with two units, 4th Detachment, anti-armour unit, and that's it?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good. And were you given the means to be able to link up with them?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: What means do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't have in mind any means. I'm asking you. Were you given the means, for example, radio, smoke signals? How were you going to link up with them?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As I've already said at the beginning of my testimony, on the bridge I was met by the anti-armour company, which was supposed to be on my right as you're looking from the direction of Bosnia-Herzegovina towards Croatia. And on the left-hand side --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I stop you? I'll ask you about this later, but all I want to know is what means were you provided to link up with these other formations, or was it a case of your order simply being: Go to the Sava and you'll be met by the 4th Detachment and the anti-armour unit?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: My order was clear, and it said that I would be met there by one unit, and that was the anti-armour company, and that they would give me the communications equipment that they had at their disposal at that time. When we came physically in contact, they gave me a Motorola. That's the name of this piece of equipment, and it worked on one frequency only, and it was the only way I could establish contact with Aco Jankovic, who was on the silo, behind my back, and he was the only person that I could establish contact with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this anti-armour company, was it part of the 4th Detachment or was it completely separate, as far as you could understand, from the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was a separate unit. It was not part of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll return to that in a moment. But if you go to paragraph 13, you say that part of your task was to "coordinate our activity with the 4th Detachment, which was already there." What specific orders or instructions did you have in order to coordinate your activities with the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The more specific orders were as follows: Since the 4th Detachment and its command and troops were in the town of Samac, I was supposed to link up from the bridge on the left-hand side and the shift that I was to receive on the bridge, because I couldn't stay there a long time, I was told that the 4th Detachment would send their troops, they would give us food, cigarettes and everything that my unit might require. That's what the commander Subotin told me and ordered me to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And no doubt about it, you were informed of this on the night of the 16th, before you set off for Bosanski Samac, before you arrived at the River Sava?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Around midnight. Yes, around midnight, on the night between the 16th and the 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. And did your commander, whoever was giving you these orders or instructions, tell you of anyone in particular that you should communicate with or liaise with in the 4th Detachment upon your arrival at the banks of the Sava?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to ask you some brief questions about your journey to Bosanski Samac. And again, it relates to paragraph 13. You say in the paragraph that "the town of Bosanski Samac was practically already blocked," and you give descriptions of the directions in which it was blocked. And you also say, I quote: "It could be said to have been completely blocked and surrounded." That's in paragraph 13. Tell the Trial Chamber how you made it through the Croatian lines to enter Bosanski Samac if it was completely blocked and surrounded.

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: When I left Obudovac, as I was leaving it, actually, I was told to move through the Serbian-held territory, because the main road from Obudovac and to Bosanski Samac was taken by the Croatian troops, and one could see them already at the beginning of the main Samac-Orasje [phoen] road . And the proposal was to go towards -- through Gornja Slatina, Kruskovac [phoen] and to exit in Crkvina, and from Crkvina towards the bridge. Those were all territories held by Serbs. The second part of Hasici, which was inhabited by the Croatian population, and between Lugovi and Kruskovo Polje, there was an anti-aircraft cannon, and it would have been very dangerous to move through there in a military truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. And you've provided already some detail in your statement about that. However, I'm interested in this: In paragraph 13, you assert that Bosanski Samac could be said to be completely -- these are your words - completely blocked and surrounded. Completely blocked and surrounded. Now, how did you get into the town if the town is completely blocked and surrounded by Croatian forces?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: But what I have just mentioned is far from the town. On one side it is about 5 to 6 kilometres from the town, and on the other side some 7 to 8 kilometres from the town. But the town itself was not blocked. Rather, at that time, Croats, wherever they were, they installed their forces there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in Bosanski Samac, did you see any evidence of civilians fleeing, weapons being fired, battles being fought, firefights in the street, exchanges of fire over the Sava, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that. But I heard things like that. Around 3.00 or somewhat later, I could hear sporadic shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll get into that later. Don't worry. But all I'm asking you is about your initial arrival. It's the case, isn't it, that you saw nothing of those matters that I mentioned when you first arrived in Bosanski Samac? That's the case, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anything. I just saw columns of vehicles, but that meant nothing to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, the population was asleep in their beds in the middle of the night, for the most part, as far as you could tell, unaware that they were completely blocked and surrounded by Croatian forces; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether they were asleep. I wasn't there, was I?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's fair enough. Thank you. You arrived and eventually made your way to the duty-free zone, and there you met two groups of soldiers: Camouflage -- soldiers in camouflage uniform and members of this anti-armour unit that you've spoken of. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it apparent to you that they were both members of two distinct military units?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were different. They were there together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So there's no way that you could arrive at any conclusion that the men in camouflage were not part of the anti-armour brigade?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I said that I had arrived and I saw that group. There were a few of them there. I don't know who they were. In any case, they were together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. As far as you could tell, one group of soldiers, some in camouflage, others not?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct. Some wore JNA uniforms and the others wore other types of uniforms, or a different type of uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The others who wore the different types of uniform, did they speak with Serbian accents?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Since I communicated with a person whom I knew personally, we just greeted each other using our customary greeting: Good luck. And that's all the communication I had with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that person gave you a Motorola and instructed you to use that for the purposes of communication with other units in the area, other JNA units in the area; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. That Motorola worked on one frequency only. I did not know of any other. And this was my only connection with the silo, with the person who was there on the silo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So tell the Chamber who informed you of the soldiers being on top of the silos.

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you find out that there were soldiers -- or there was someone on top of the silo?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I found out from soldiers who gave me that piece of communication equipment, and they told me that my only communication at that moment was with the man who was on top of the silo. We established contact, we checked the communication lines, and the communication lines worked, and that's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did they explain to you who the man on the silo was from -- who he was, rather, and which military unit of the JNA he was from?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They told me who he was. I knew the man personally. And everything was clear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the man Aco Jankovic, from the 1st Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you been informed, prior to going to the Sava, taking up your positions, that the 1st Detachment was also going to be conducting operations that night? Did you expect them to be there?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Before I left Obudovac, I was told that our forces, our army, the JNA, should take up the silos and that we should also establish communication with them. They were supposed to take up the silos, but I don't know which -- I didn't know, rather, at the time which unit that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you informed that the 1st, 2nd, or 3rd Detachments would be conducting operations in Bosanski Samac that night?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't informed. I was only told about the anti-armour company. And as I've already told you, I was not informed what units or what troops were going to be there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You describe in your statement some exchanges of fire that took place on the night of the 16th and 17th. Essentially, you describe two exchanges, firstly a mortar attack on the vicinity of your positions and the silos; and secondly, an exchange of fire with small -- light arms, I assume, over the bridge towards the Sava. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry. Is now the time that we break, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, and we'll continue at 1415 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio, you continue. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the night of the 16th and 17th, how -- how far were your positions on the Sava from the SUP building in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as the crow flies, between 300 and 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear the sound of any explosions or armed or small arms fire from the vicinity of the police station?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know that that was the paramilitaries taking control of the police station, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was not aware of that. I heard sounds of shooting but I didn't know who that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You subsequently found out, though, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I found out that there had been a shootout outside the police station, that there were armed clashes. I can't remember who exactly was involved in these clashes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the -- you know that a Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac was established and started governing Bosanski Samac, the municipality, from about the 17th onwards?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, I was on the line and I was not aware of what was happening in the town, or who had taken over power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you subsequently found out, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you knew, and I suggest to you, at the time, that this Serbian municipality had been -- had declared itself sometime earlier in March at least of 1992.

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I was a soldier. I didn't know about these things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that there were Serbian police, there was a Serbian police force, headed by Stevan Todorovic, in existence on the night of the 16th and 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: SIMO JOVANOVIC
